consensus: GTCT / AGAC (palindrome GTCTAGAC); also the 5-bp GC motif GGC(GC/CG)
short: SMAD proteins are the intracellular effectors of TGF-beta family signaling. Their MH1 domain inserts a beta-hairpin into the major groove and reads just four bases, GTCT or its reverse complement AGAC, often written as the CAGAC box or as the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC. SMAD3, SMAD4 and the BMP-activated SMAD1/5/9 also bind a separate 5-bp GC-rich element, GGCGC or GGCCG. Both elements are far too short to be informative alone, and genome-wide SMAD occupancy is set mainly by whichever lineage-determining factor is present, so most SMAD ChIP peaks are better explained by a partner's motif than by an SBE. This is a family where a motif hit needs corroboration more than almost any other.
long:
## The factors

Eight human SMADs fall into three groups. The receptor-regulated R-SMADs are SMAD2 and SMAD3
(phosphorylated by TGF-beta and activin receptors) and SMAD1, SMAD5 and SMAD9/SMAD8
(phosphorylated by BMP receptors). SMAD4 is the shared co-SMAD. SMAD6 and SMAD7 are inhibitory
and are not sequence-specific activators. DNA contact is made by the N-terminal MH1 domain, a
compact domain with a bound zinc ion whose 11-residue beta-hairpin inserts into the major groove [PMID:9741623];
the C-terminal MH2 domain mediates trimerization, so the functional unit on DNA is normally a
trimer of two R-SMADs plus SMAD4, giving two or three DNA-contacting hairpins [PMID:29234012]. One paralogue is a
special case: wild-type SMAD2 carries a 30-residue insert encoded by exon 3 immediately before the
hairpin that blocks direct DNA binding [PMID:9873005]. Full-length SMAD2 reaches DNA through partners, most
clearly the forkhead protein FOXH1/FAST1 [PMID:9702197,9873005]; the naturally occurring SMAD2 delta-exon-3 splice form
does bind DNA, like SMAD3 [PMID:9873005].

## The motif

The classical Smad-binding element is 4 bp, GTCT, read on the other strand as AGAC and usually
quoted with a flanking base as CAGAC ("CAGA box") or CAGACA. Zawel and colleagues showed that
SMAD3 and SMAD4 both recognize an identical 8-bp palindrome, GTCTAGAC [PMID:9660945], and the Smad3 MH1 crystal
structure explained why: the hairpin reads GTCT and two hairpins from a trimer can occupy the two
halves of the palindrome [PMID:9741623]. Real promoters usually contain tandem CAGA repeats rather than a perfect
palindrome; the TGF-beta response element of the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter is the canonical example [PMID:9606191].
Separately, SMADs bind a 5-bp GC-rich element with consensus GGC(GC) or GGC(CG). This was first
described as a BMP-responsive element for SMAD1/5 [PMID:10679014], but structural work showed that SMAD3 and SMAD4
bind the same 5GC motifs, and that these motifs occur in clusters in SMAD-bound regions
genome-wide [PMID:29234012]. So the family has two chemically distinct consensus sequences, not one; a database
entry showing GTCTAGAC and one showing a GC-rich string can both be correct. The data for this
family reflects that split, and its cohesion (0.76) is the lowest in this batch. The CAGAC-type
and 5GC-type models do not interconvert, and paralogues are not separable from sequence within
either type. The CIS-BP SMAD9 entry is a GC-rich model transferred from a Drosophila protein at
91% MH1 identity, not a human measurement.

## Where it acts

SMAD sites are distributed across promoters and enhancers with no CpG-island preference for the
CAGAC form, while 5GC clusters are by definition GC-rich and promoter-biased. What matters more is
that SMAD occupancy is almost entirely conditional. Smad3 ChIP-seq in three different cell types
recovers three largely non-overlapping site sets, each co-occupied by that cell type's
lineage-determining factor: OCT4 in embryonic stem cells, MYOD1 in myotubes, PU.1 in pro-B cells [PMID:22036565].
In other systems the recurring partners are FOXH1 and other forkhead proteins, RUNX1/2, AP-1
(JUN/FOS), TEAD, and the repressors TGIF1, SKI and SnoN. Named composite elements include the
activin-responsive element of the Mix.2 promoter (a forkhead site next to a SMAD site) [PMID:9702197,9873005] and the
BMP-responsive elements of the Id1 and Smad7 promoters. In practice a SMAD peak set looks like the
partner's peak set with a weak SBE enrichment layered on top.

## Biology and disease

TGF-beta/BMP signaling through SMADs controls epithelial growth arrest, extracellular matrix
production, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, regulatory T cell induction, bone and cartilage
formation, and left-right and dorsoventral patterning. Smad3-null mice die within months from
impaired mucosal immunity with defective T cell responses to TGF-beta [PMID:10064594]. SMAD4 was identified as
DPC4, a candidate tumor suppressor at 18q21.1 that was homozygously deleted in 25 of 84 pancreatic
carcinomas (about 30%), with potentially inactivating mutations in 6 of 27 of the others [PMID:8553070]; germline SMAD4 mutations cause juvenile polyposis and, with an overlapping
phenotype, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia [PMID:9582123,15031030]. SMAD4 and SMAD2/SMAD3 are also recurrently
mutated in colorectal cancer, and loss of SMAD signaling converts TGF-beta from a growth
suppressor to a driver of invasion and immune evasion [PMID:37714133]. SMAD9 mutations cause a form of pulmonary
arterial hypertension, consistent with the BMP9/BMPR2 axis [PMID:19211612].

## Reading a hit

Treat an isolated SBE match as essentially no evidence. GTCT or AGAC occurs about once every 128
bases on either strand, so a 4-bp core appears tens of millions of times in the human genome; even
the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC is expected tens of thousands of times by chance. A SMAD hit becomes
meaningful only in one of three forms: several CAGA repeats within a short window, a cluster of
5GC motifs, or an SBE within a few base pairs of a validated partner site (a forkhead, RUNX,
AP-1 or TEAD motif). The second problem is that ChIP-derived SMAD motifs in these collections are
contaminated by indirect binding almost by construction, since SMAD complexes are recruited by
lineage factors. Every HOCOMOCO SMAD2 model here rests on ChIP-seq only (evidence code P), and
wild-type SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly [PMID:9873005], so those matrices describe the composition of SMAD2
peaks rather than SMAD2's own specificity. Finally, do not use a hit to name a paralogue. CAGAC
does not mean TGF-beta rather than BMP, because SMAD1/5 bind CAGAC-type sites too and SMAD3/4 bind
GC-type sites; the original "TGF-beta uses CAGAC, BMP uses GC" division does not survive the
structural and genome-wide data [PMID:29234012,33510867].
caveats: The lowest-confidence family in this batch. A 4-bp SBE is not a finding; even the 8-bp palindrome is common by chance. The family has two unrelated consensus sequences (CAGAC-type and 5GC-type), so conflicting database entries may both be right, and paralogues are not separable within either. Most SMAD ChIP peaks are explained by a partner's motif, not by an SBE, and all HOCOMOCO SMAD2 models here are ChIP-only while full-length SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly. The CIS-BP SMAD9 model is transferred from Drosophila. Use SMAD hits only as supporting evidence alongside a partner site or experimental occupancy.

timeline.finding: SMAD3 and SMAD4 each recognize the same 8-bp palindrome, GTCTAGAC, and tandem copies confer TGF-beta responsiveness that is lost in SMAD4-deleted cells, establishing SMADs as sequence-specific DNA-binding factors.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection from random oligonucleotides, reporter assays, SMAD4-null cells

timeline.finding: Three CAGA boxes in the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter are bound directly by SMAD3 and SMAD4, are required for TGF-beta induction, and respond to TGF-beta and activin but not BMP; recombinant SMAD1 and SMAD2 do not bind them.
timeline.methods: Promoter mutagenesis, EMSA with recombinant proteins and nuclear extracts, reporter assays
timeline.open: What, if anything, the BMP-activated SMADs bind directly.

timeline.finding: The 2.8 A structure of the SMAD3 MH1 domain on DNA shows that base-specific recognition is made entirely by a conserved 11-residue beta-hairpin in the major groove.

Wild-type SMAD2 does not bind DNA directly because of the exon 3 insert before the hairpin; it reaches target promoters with SMAD4 through the forkhead partner FAST/FOXH1, whereas the delta-exon-3 isoform and SMAD3 bind DNA themselves.

BMP-activated SMAD1 with SMAD4 binds the GC-rich GCCGnCGC element first defined for Drosophila Mad, weakly and only with multiple repeats, and GCCG reporters respond to BMP but not TGF-beta, supporting a split between GC-type BMP sites and CAGA-type TGF-beta sites.
timeline.open: Whether the GC versus CAGA division reflected intrinsic specificity or the reporter contexts tested.

timeline.finding: SMAD3 ChIP-seq in embryonic stem cells, myotubes and pro-B cells gives largely distinct site sets, each co-occupied with and dependent on that cell's lineage-determining factor (OCT4, MYOD1, PU.1); inducing MYOD1 redirects SMAD3.

Structures of SMAD3 and SMAD4 on goosecoid promoter DNA define the 5-bp GC motif GGC(GC)|(CG) as a site for TGF-beta-activated, BMP-activated and common SMADs alike, and 5GC clusters are frequent in SMAD-bound regions genome-wide. This overturns the view that CAGAC is the TGF-beta site and GC-rich elements the BMP site.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, binding assays, ChIP-seq motif analysis

timeline.finding: SMAD5 and SMAD8 MH1 structures show all MH1 domains bind 5GC motifs similarly, but SMAD2/3/4 MH1 domains bind as monomers while SMAD1/5/8 form helix-swapped dimers, and site clustering and spacing in ChIP-seq peaks differ between BMP- and TGF-beta-responsive genes.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, NMR, chimeric domains, ChIP-seq motif analysis
timeline.open: Whether monomer-versus-dimer propensity actually drives pathway-specific target selection in cells.

open: How TGF-beta and BMP SMADs reach different targets is unresolved now that both bind CAGAC-type and 5GC sites: one proposal is that MH1 monomer (SMAD2/3/4) versus helix-swapped dimer (SMAD1/5/8) propensity sets site spacing and clustering, the alternative is that partner factors such as FOXH1 or lineage-determining factors choose the sites and the SMAD motif contributes little.

The ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO SMAD2, SMAD3 and SMAD4 models (for example tGTCTGdCACc and AGGTGncAGACA) do not match the in vitro palindrome GTCTAGAC, and it is not settled whether they describe composite SMAD-partner sites or simply peak composition shaped by recruiting factors.
